colorRules.accentUsage: Use the deep teal accent as the primary action and interaction color: main CTAs, selected navigation states, links, focus rings, progress indicators, and concise financial status highlights. Keep it purposeful and repeatable, with no more than 3-7 accent moments visible in a screen. Prefer accent text or borders over large decorative fills; reserve solid accent fills for high-priority actions and compact controls.
colorRules.semanticUsage: Use success, warning, danger, and info as functional financial signals rather than decoration. Apply them through small badges, status labels, inline messages, table indicators, tinted backgrounds, and restrained borders. Pair every semantic color with clear text or an icon so meaning never depends on color alone. Keep semantic treatments visually quieter than the primary teal action system.
colorRules.neutralUsage: Build most of the interface from the pale blue-green neutral system. Use the lightest neutrals for the app background and raised surfaces, middle neutrals for subtle overlays and dividers, and the darkest neutrals for primary text. Use secondary and muted neutrals for supporting labels, metadata, helper text, and inactive navigation. Keep borders low-contrast and use the raised surface to create hierarchy instead of heavy shadows.
forbiddenPatterns: Do not use more than one accent hue in a screen or introduce generic blue, indigo, purple, or neon fintech colors.
Do not use the teal accent as a full-page background, decorative blob, oversized illustration field, or repeated card fill.
Do not use gradients on cards, sections, surfaces, or financial data panels.
Do not use pure black or pure white; preserve the warm blue-green neutral atmosphere.
Do not communicate financial status through color alone or use semantic colors for purely decorative emphasis.

typographyRules.displayUsage: Use Sora as the single brand typeface for product headings, account balances, navigation labels, buttons, onboarding copy, and prominent financial summaries. Its geometric form should make money management feel approachable and confident without becoming childish. Use sentence case for headings and labels.
typographyRules.bodyUsage: Use Sora at a minimum of 16px for body copy, form inputs, transaction descriptions, explanatory content, and primary data labels. Keep copy direct, practical, and friendly for people learning to manage money. Use 14px only for compact metadata, table support text, and secondary labels.
typographyRules.monoUsage: Use IBM Plex Mono only for technical or precision-oriented content such as account identifiers, transaction references, exchange rates, timestamps, code-like values, and tabular numeric details where alignment improves scanning. Do not use it for general body copy or headlines.
typographyRules.weightRules: Use 400 for body copy and standard data. Use 500 for navigation, labels, buttons, and lightly emphasized values. Use 600 for section headings, active states, and important financial summaries. Use 700 sparingly for major page headings or hero balances. Never use 200, 300, 800, or 900, and never bold an entire paragraph.
typographyRules.sizeRules: Use 16px/24px as the default readable body size. Use 14px/20px for compact metadata and 12px/16px for captions only when they are nonessential. Use 20px-30px for component and section headings, 36px-48px for major app headings or prominent balance figures, and 48px/52px only for a single high-priority financial headline. Maintain clear size contrast without making every number oversized.

spacingRules.sectionMargins: Use the 4px-based spacing scale with 48px-96px vertical separation between major app regions and up to 128px only for major onboarding or narrative moments. Vary spacing by hierarchy rather than giving every section the same height. Keep the desktop experience inside a centered 1280px container with a functional sidebar and content area.
spacingRules.componentPadding: Use 16px horizontal and 12px vertical padding for compact rows, inputs, navigation items, and transaction entries. Use 24px horizontal and 16px vertical padding for relaxed panels and key summaries. Use 32px padding for primary account overviews or onboarding surfaces. Maintain comfortable touch targets and avoid dense, spreadsheet-like compression.
spacingRules.rhythmDescription: Follow an airy but balanced 4px/8px rhythm: enough whitespace to make unfamiliar financial information approachable, with tighter grouping inside transaction rows, forms, and summaries. Establish hierarchy through spacing, surface contrast, and dividers rather than excessive cards. Prefer lists, tables, and structured rows over card grids, with no more than three prominent cards visible at once.

motionRules.transitions: Use color and border transitions for hover, focus, selected, and validation states. Use subtle opacity changes for reveals and confirmations, and short transform transitions for drawers, expanding details, and layout changes. Animate balances or progress only when the change communicates a real financial update; avoid playful motion that could distract from money-related decisions.
motionRules.easing: Use the standard cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1) curve for a smooth, controlled ease-out feel. Motion should feel responsive and polished rather than bouncy or game-like, reinforcing trust while retaining the brand's playful clarity.
motionRules.duration: Use 120ms for hover, focus, pressed, and icon micro-interactions; 200ms for control state changes, validation, navigation selection, and row expansion; and 320ms for drawers, page-level reveals, and meaningful layout transitions. Respect reduced-motion preferences and remove nonessential movement when requested.

signatureMoves: Present money with bold, highly legible Sora figures paired with small, precise IBM Plex Mono details for a friendly but trustworthy fintech contrast.
Use deep teal as a concentrated action signal: one clear primary action, restrained selected states, and crisp focus rings rather than broad decorative color.
Structure the app around a persistent desktop sidebar and calm, pale blue-green surfaces so new users can scan balances, activity, and next actions without visual overload.
Use raised transaction and account rows with subtle borders, compact status badges, and occasional accent edge treatments instead of a grid of generic cards.
Pair playful, plainspoken microcopy with disciplined spacing and precise financial labels, making unfamiliar money tasks feel understandable without losing seriousness.
antiPatterns: Do not use centered marketing-style hero layouts, footer navigation, or tabbars in the desktop app; prioritize sidebar-led, function-first navigation.
Do not use dense dashboards filled with tiny text, excessive charts, or more than three prominent cards in a viewport.
Do not use gradients, floating blobs, abstract decorative shapes, confetti-like effects, or gamified motion around financial decisions.
Do not pair competing primary buttons, vague calls to action, or generic motivational copy with money-management workflows.
Do not use oversized all-caps labels, full-paragraph bold text, circular-avatar testimonial patterns, or unstructured card carousels.
